territorial_scope.description: Applies to data center and web search portal businesses in Iowa; eligibility requires a physical location in the state.

evidence.quote: The data center business shall have a physical location in the state

summary.short: Iowa Code §423.3 lists sales and use tax exemptions. Subsection 95 exempts computers, equipment, backup power fuel and electricity used by data center businesses that invest at least $200 million in Iowa within six years and register annually with the department.
summary.long: Iowa Code §423.3 lists exemptions from the state sales and use tax, including resales, agricultural inputs, nonprofit purchases, food, medicine and manufacturing inputs. Subsections 92, 93 and 95 are its data-center provisions. Subsection 95 exempts the sales price of computers and equipment, cooling and power infrastructure, backup power generation fuel and electricity used by a data center business; subsections 92 and 93 apply similar exemptions to web search portal businesses. The exemption applies from the initial investment or site preparation. A data center business needs a physical location in Iowa of at least 5,000 square feet, a $200 million minimum investment in an Iowa location within six years, registration with the department, an annual report from January 31, 2026, and compliance with sustainable design standards. Fuel and electricity exemption duration depends on whether the property began operating before June 6, 2025 and, for later property, on whether it lies in a city over 30,000 residents (ten years) or elsewhere (fifteen years). If less than 80% of the minimum investment is made within six years, the exemption is lost and the tax due, plus penalty and interest, is owed.

notes: The document is the full Iowa Code section 423.3, printed 12 Dec 2025 as Iowa Code 2026; these fields cover subsection 95 only. Subsections 92, 93 and 95 use near-identical language, but 95 adds a 5,000 square foot physical location requirement (95(b)(2)) and a lease-term start date (95(b)(3), (c), (d)), and only 95 requires compliance with section 103A.8B standards. Wording differs between paragraphs: 95(a)(2)(b)(iii) says 'not located entirely or in part within a city', while 95(a)(3)(b)(iii) says 'not located in part within a city'. The text does not name the department and gives no penalty amounts for failing the 80% investment test in 95(e), which refers only to penalty and interest imposed by statute. The 2025 history note is not tied to subsection 95 specifically. Filing dates (January 31, 2026 and annually) are events and are not coded here.
